title: Getting Started
text: package ships synthetic dataset, erglm_data, used throughout documentation. exposure metric (aucss), several covariates (sex, age, weight, dose, …), response columns supported family: binary (ae1, ae2), count (ae_count), continuous (biomarker_change), positive right-skewed continuous (ae_duration):

title: Getting Started
text: erglm_model() fits model – takes formula/data arguments glm(), plus family argument (defaulting gaussian(), matching glm()’s default):
code: mod <- erglm_model(ae1 ~ aucss + sex, erglm_data, family = binomial()) mod #>  #> Call:  stats::glm(formula = formula, family = family, data = data) #>  #> Coefficients: #> (Intercept)        aucss      sexMale   #>   -1.648112     0.005508    -0.312234   #>  #> Degrees of Freedom: 299 Total (i.e. Null);  297 Residual #> Null Deviance:       402.1  #> Residual Deviance: 192.7     AIC: 198.7

title: Getting Started
text: several candidate covariates, erglm_scm_forward() erglm_scm_backward() automate process deciding belong model, via stepwise addition/elimination based significance testing: See “Stepwise covariate modelling” article full treatment, including forward/backward workflow audit log (erglm_scm_history()).

title: Using base R model methods
text: Base R’s plot.lm() diagnostic plots (plot(mod, = 1:4)) also work, though panels (e.g. leverage) informative continuous responses binary ones. erglm deliberately doesn’t provide diagnostic plotting – see companion erplots package exposure-response-specific visualisations.

title: Stepwise covariate modelling
text: lowest level, covariate modelling just adding removing single term fitted model. Two exported helpers exactly , erglm_add_term() erglm_remove_term(), taking one-sided formula naming term returning refitted model: stepwise functions built top : repeatedly propose add/remove moves, compare candidate current model significance testing (anova()), keep best one. rarely need call erglm_add_term()/erglm_remove_term() directly, ’s worth knowing ’re automated search hood.
code: base_mod <- erglm_model(ae1 ~ aucss, erglm_data, family = binomial())  erglm_add_term(base_mod, ~ sex) #>  #> Call:  stats::glm(formula = formula, family = family, data = data) #>  #> Coefficients: #> (Intercept)        aucss      sexMale   #>    -1.64811      0.00551     -0.31223   #>  #> Degrees of Freedom: 299 Total (i.e. Null);  297 Residual #> Null Deviance:       402  #> Residual Deviance: 193   AIC: 199

title: Stepwise covariate modelling
text: Two ingredients needed drive SCM run: base model start , character vector candidate covariates consider. Unlike covariate-modelling frameworks, candidates don’t need tied particular structural parameter – ’re just term names added (removed ) right-hand side model formula:
code: candidates <- c("sex", "dose", "weight", "age")

title: Stepwise covariate modelling
text: Every candidate already model added turn compared current model; term smallest pp-value retained, provided pp-value threshold. step repeats remaining candidate clears bar: None four candidates clear default 0.010.01 threshold – inspecting history shows : sex genuine (modest) effect ae1 data-generating process behind erglm_data, aucss already model effect isn’t strong enough, sample size, clear 0.010.01 threshold – search correctly leaves rather adding covariate doesn’t earn place.
code: fwd_mod <- erglm_scm_forward(base_mod, candidates, threshold = 0.01, seed = 3425) fwd_mod$formula #> ae1 ~ aucss erglm_scm_history(fwd_mod)[, c("term_tested", "term_p_value", "model_updated")] #>   term_tested term_p_value model_updated #> 1        <NA>           NA            NA #> 2        ~sex      0.39063             0 #> 3     ~weight      0.06218             0 #> 4        ~age      0.17665             0 #> 5       ~dose      0.70247             0

title: Stepwise covariate modelling
text: Backward elimination works reverse: term currently model dropped turn, term largest pp-value removed pp-value exceeds threshold. see real work, start saturated model already contains every candidate: four candidates pruned, leaving aucss – matching forward addition already told us: none sex, dose, weight, age earns place model thresholds. full audit log shows iteration--iteration elimination: iteration removes single worst-performing term (model_updated == 1); next iteration re-tests everything still model, since removing one term can change others’ apparent significance. thresholds differ. ’s standard practice make forward addition permissive backward elimination – 0.010.01 add 0.0010.001 retain. term added looser forward criterion must survive stricter backward criterion, guards terms looked useful presence others. Keeping backward threshold forward threshold also prevents procedure cycling (adding removing term forever). Reproducibility. Within step, candidate terms tested random order, results can depend state random number generator; passing seed makes run reproducible. seed omitted, random one chosen reported via message.
code: full_mod <- erglm_model(ae1 ~ aucss + sex + dose + weight + age, erglm_data, family = binomial()) bwd_mod <- erglm_scm_backward(full_mod, candidates, threshold = 0.001, seed = 9821) bwd_mod$formula #> ae1 ~ aucss #> attr(,"variables") #> list(ae1, aucss) #> attr(,"factors") #>       aucss #> ae1       0 #> aucss     1 #> attr(,"term.labels") #> [1] "aucss" #> attr(,"order") #> [1] 1 #> attr(,"intercept") #> [1] 1 #> attr(,"response") #> [1] 1 #> attr(,".Environment") #> <environment: R_GlobalEnv> #> attr(,"predvars") #> list(ae1, aucss) #> attr(,"dataClasses") #>       ae1     aucss  #> "numeric" "numeric" print(   erglm_scm_history(bwd_mod)[, c("iteration", "term_tested", "term_p_value", "model_updated")],   row.names = FALSE ) #>  iteration term_tested term_p_value model_updated #>          0        <NA>           NA            NA #>          1        ~sex      0.86307             1 #>          1       ~dose      0.84535             0 #>          1        ~age      0.12318             0 #>          1     ~weight      0.07129             0 #>          2     ~weight      0.04418             0 #>          2        ~age      0.12348             0 #>          2       ~dose      0.85135             1 #>          3        ~age      0.11832             1 #>          3     ~weight      0.04309             0 #>          4     ~weight      0.06218             1

title: Stepwise covariate modelling
text: default, step selects term using pp-value approach described . Pass criterion = "aic" criterion = "bic" select instead strict improvement information criterion: term added (forward) removed (backward) strictly decreases AIC/BIC relative current model, candidate producing largest improvement wins. threshold ignored criterion isn’t "p-value", term_p_value left NA history, since significance test plays role selection. AIC permissive default pp-value threshold, forward addition criterion = "aic" finds covariates worth adding pp-value search found none: history’s criterion column records selection rule drove step (NA base-model row), term_p_value NA throughout since isn’t used . model_aic model_bic always populated regardless criterion, search driven one criterion can still audited . criterion argument works erglm_scm_backward():
code: aic_mod <- erglm_scm_forward(base_mod, candidates, criterion = "aic", seed = 3425) aic_mod$formula #> ae1 ~ aucss + weight + age #> <environment: 0x555daa54d178> erglm_scm_history(aic_mod)[, c("term_tested", "criterion", "term_p_value", "model_aic", "model_updated")] #>    term_tested criterion term_p_value model_aic model_updated #> 1         <NA>      <NA>           NA     197.4            NA #> 2         ~sex       aic           NA     198.7             0 #> 3      ~weight       aic           NA     195.9             1 #> 4         ~age       aic           NA     197.6             0 #> 5        ~dose       aic           NA     199.3             0 #> 6         ~age       aic           NA     195.5             1 #> 7         ~sex       aic           NA     197.9             0 #> 8        ~dose       aic           NA     197.8             0 #> 9         ~sex       aic           NA     197.5             0 #> 10       ~dose       aic           NA     197.5             0 bic_mod <- erglm_scm_backward(full_mod, candidates, criterion = "bic", seed = 9821) bic_mod$formula #> ae1 ~ aucss #> attr(,"variables") #> list(ae1, aucss) #> attr(,"factors") #>       aucss #> ae1       0 #> aucss     1 #> attr(,"term.labels") #> [1] "aucss" #> attr(,"order") #> [1] 1 #> attr(,"intercept") #> [1] 1 #> attr(,"response") #> [1] 1 #> attr(,".Environment") #> <environment: R_GlobalEnv> #> attr(,"predvars") #> list(ae1, aucss) #> attr(,"dataClasses") #>       ae1     aucss  #> "numeric" "numeric"

title: Stepwise covariate modelling
text: typical workflow forward-backward run: forward addition build model , immediately followed backward elimination prune . functions take fitted model first argument return fitted model, compose naturally pipe: Since forward addition already found nothing worth adding, backward elimination nothing left prune, pipeline settles base model. final_mod ordinary fitted model object, usual methods apply – summary(), confint(), predict(), behave normally.
code: final_mod <- base_mod |>   erglm_scm_forward(candidates, threshold = 0.01, seed = 3425) |>   erglm_scm_backward(candidates, threshold = 0.001, seed = 9821)  final_mod$formula #> ae1 ~ aucss

title: Stepwise covariate modelling
text: Selection criterion. default pp-value selection (criterion = "p-value"); pass criterion = "aic" criterion = "bic" select information criterion instead. history records model_aic model_bic every candidate regardless criterion active, can always audit search criteria didn’t use drive . Threshold choice. forward backward thresholds main levers control. Stricter thresholds yield sparser models. Greediness. Stepwise search greedy isn’t guaranteed find globally best subset covariates – , article’s example shows, may correctly find candidate covariates belong model given sample size threshold. audit log valuable precisely makes path search took transparent reproducible.

title: Simulation
text: Calling simulate() generates one replicate datasets. number replicates set nsim, seed can supplied reproducibility:

title: Simulation
text: Generating replicate involves two distinct sources randomness, simulate() accounts : Parameter uncertainty. fresh parameter vector drawn multivariate normal distribution implied estimates covariance matrix, using coef(mod) vcov(mod). represents uncertain fitted parameters . Observation noise. Given parameter draw, expected response μi\mu_i evaluated observation’s exposure covariates, response generated around . noise model family-appropriate: Bernoulli draws binomial, Poisson draws poisson, normal draws gaussian (), gamma draws Gamma. sources included, simulated val column behaves like genuine new dataset drawn fitted model, merely noiseless prediction.

title: Simulation
text: result tidy, long-format data frame nsim×\timesnobs rows: columns : dat_id – index identifying original observation (row data). sim_id – replicate row belongs (1 nsim). mu – expected response (response scale) observation sampled parameters. val – simulated response (mean plus family-appropriate noise). sampled coefficient values, prefixed coef_* (e.g. coef_`(Intercept)`, coef_aucss) avoid colliding predictor columns name, repeated across rows replicate – one parameter draw used per replicate. model’s predictor columns (aucss), carried along can group plot exposure covariates. Requesting several replicates stacks , sampled coefficients vary one replicate next staying constant within replicate:
code: names(sim1) #> [1] "dat_id"           "sim_id"           "mu"               "val"              #> [5] "coef_(Intercept)" "coef_aucss"       "aucss" sims <- simulate(mod, nsim = 50, seed = 1) dim(sims) #> [1] 15000     7  # one parameter draw per replicate unique(sims[sims$sim_id <= 3, c("sim_id", "coef_(Intercept)", "coef_aucss")]) #>     sim_id coef_(Intercept) coef_aucss #> 1        1           -1.716   0.001900 #> 301      2           -1.740   0.002017 #> 601      3           -1.606   0.001764

title: Simulation
text: simulate() bundles parameter sampling noise generation together, erglm_fun() exposes deterministic core: prediction function . returns function two arguments, param data, default values used model fitted: control arguments, can evaluate model situations original fit never saw. Supplying param lets ask counterfactual “parameters different?” questions – example, setting intercept zero: Supplying data lets evaluate curve exposures covariate values choosing – instance, tracing exposure-response relationship grid aucss values: default erglm_fun() returns predictions response scale (type = "response"); pass type = "link" link scale.

title: Simulation
text: erglm_fun() tool reach simulate() doesn’t exactly need want assemble pieces . illustration, can build exposure-response curve parameter-uncertainty band combining erglm_fun() manual parameter draw – reproducing, lower level, parameter-sampling step simulate() performs internally. recipe : draw many parameter vectors estimated sampling distribution, evaluate curve exposure grid draw, summarise resulting family curves pointwise.  band reflects parameter uncertainty, summarised mean curve never added residual noise – ’s analogue confidence band. Adding step draws rnorm(..., sd = sqrt(summary(mod)$dispersion)) around evaluated mean turn prediction band also captures observation noise, precisely extra ingredient simulate() supplies . essential trade-two tools: simulate() convenient complete, erglm_fun() transparent fully control.
code: set.seed(1) n_draws <- 500 draws <- mvtnorm::rmvnorm(n_draws, mean = coef(mod), sigma = vcov(mod)) colnames(draws) <- names(coef(mod))  curve_grid <- data.frame(aucss = seq(0, max(erglm_data$aucss), length.out = 100))  # evaluate the curve for every parameter draw curves <- apply(draws, 1, function(p) f(data = curve_grid, param = p))  # summarise pointwise across draws band <- data.frame(   aucss = curve_grid$aucss,   fit = f(data = curve_grid),   lwr = apply(curves, 1, stats::quantile, probs = 0.025),   upr = apply(curves, 1, stats::quantile, probs = 0.975) )  ggplot(band, aes(aucss)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), fill = "firebrick", alpha = 0.2) +   geom_line(aes(y = fit), colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 1) +   labs(x = "AUCss", y = "Mean biomarker change", subtitle = "Point estimate with 95% parameter-uncertainty band")

what: The same tools across other glm() families
title: Simulation
text: tools work unchanged families erglm supports; noise model scale differ. binomial model, mu fitted probability val 0/1 outcome drawn Bernoulli(μ)\text{Bernoulli}(\mu): Poisson model, val drawn Poisson(μ)\text{Poisson}(\mu) always non-negative integer: Everything else – custom parameter values, custom data grids, building simulations top prediction function – carries exactly gaussian case.
code: mod_b <- erglm_model(ae1 ~ aucss + sex, erglm_data, family = binomial())  sim_b <- simulate(mod_b, nsim = 2, seed = 1) sort(unique(sim_b$val)) #> [1] 0 1  f_b <- erglm_fun(mod_b) range(f_b()) #> [1] 0.1234 1.0000 mod_p <- erglm_model(ae_count ~ aucss + sex, erglm_data, family = poisson())  sim_p <- simulate(mod_p, nsim = 2, seed = 1) all(sim_p$val == round(sim_p$val)) && all(sim_p$val >= 0) #> [1] TRUE

erglm (development version)
text: bundled erglm_data dataset’s continuous columns (aucss, cmaxss, biomarker_change, ae_duration) now rounded two decimal places, realistic degree precision; underlying values otherwise unchanged. erglm longer depends rlang, withr, tibble, dplyr (mvtnorm remains runtime dependency besides base stats). result, erglm_predict(), simulate.erglm_model(), bundled erglm_data dataset now return/plain data frames rather tibbles, erglm_predict()’s fit_link/se_link/fit_resp columns lose observation-index names used carry predict.glm() artifact; underlying values otherwise unchanged. tibble also dropped Suggests entirely, since vignettes now build example data plain data.frame() calls . erglm_scm_forward()/erglm_scm_backward() gain criterion argument, supporting "aic"/"bic"-based term selection addition existing "p-value" default. SCM history (erglm_scm_history()) gains criterion column recording selection rule applied forward/backward step (#7). Fixed several documentation gaps across help pages, vignettes, README: missing descriptions, undocumented argument defaults, broken cross-references, including several references erplots’ er_vpc_plot(), replaced er_vpc_add_simulated().

title: erglm 0.1.0
text: Initial CRAN release. Model fitting prediction exposure-response models based glm() (erglm_model(), erglm_predict()), supporting arbitrary glm() families; binomial, poisson, gaussian, gamma tested officially supported end end (fitting, prediction, SCM significance testing, simulation). Stepwise covariate modelling (erglm_scm_forward(), erglm_scm_backward(), erglm_scm_history()), built single-term erglm_add_term()/erglm_remove_term() helpers. Simulation support (erglm_fun(), simulate.erglm_model()) drawing replicate responses fitted model, sampled coefficients expected simulated response columns. Interoperability companion erplots package via er_predict()/er_simulate()/er_summary() methods, registered lazily erglm hard dependency erplots plotting package. erglm_link()/erglm_invlink(), discoverable wrappers around fitted model’s link inverse-link functions. example dataset, erglm_data, binary, count, continuous/right-skewed continuous response columns demonstrating supported family.
